_comment: G3 v0.1 acceptance gate fixture — Production Evidence binary check incl. ≥30% non-LLM-direct (paste detection). Each case carries plan + response + recentAssistantMessages + expected_passed + expected_paste_detected. Runner: scripts/g3-production-baseline.cjs.
_pass_criteria: 5/5 cases match expected_passed AND expected_paste_detected. If any mismatch, tune PASTE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD in scoring.js (currently 0.70).

cases.name: 1-genuine-artifact-no-similar-llm
cases._intent: Real production artifact unrelated to LLM messages → must pass.

plan.objective: Identify the inputs and outputs of a workflow step.

micro_proof.stimulus: List the input + output fields of one workflow step in your project.
micro_proof.expected_signal: Response contains: order_id, sku, quantity, stock_remaining, decision.
micro_proof.fail_mode: vague nouns / no field names / no decision

cases.response:
inputs:
- order_id: uuid
- sku: string (product key)
- quantity: int (requested)
outputs:
- stock_remaining: int (after reserve)
- decision: enum {accept, partial, reject} based on stock_remaining ≥ quantity.
recentAssistantMessages: Have you tried sketching the inputs and outputs of one step on paper? Pick a step you can describe in 2 minutes.
Remember the goal is to map fields, not to write code yet.

cases.name: 2-genuine-prose-different-from-llm
cases._intent: Real artifact in different shape → must pass.

micro_proof.stimulus: Describe the 3 layers of your auth system using bullet points with one role per layer.
micro_proof.expected_signal: Response contains: handler, validator, persister, plus role per layer.
micro_proof.fail_mode: skipped layers / role mixed / no separators

cases.response:
- handler: receives the http request, parses headers, hands off to validator. owns request lifecycle.
- validator: checks token signature against public-key cache, refreshes from JWKS on miss. zero state mutation.
- persister: stores last-seen timestamp + risk-score in postgres. write-only from this path.
recentAssistantMessages: An auth system typically separates request handling, validation, and persistence into distinct layers.

cases.name: 3-genuine-list-different-words
cases._intent: Real artifact with field names from prompt but different prose → must pass.

micro_proof.stimulus: Write the input + output of order processing.

cases.response:
inputs go in:
order_id (uuid v4 from gateway)
sku (varchar 32, FK to product)
quantity (positive int, hard cap 999)

outputs come out:
stock_remaining (int, may be negative if oversold path)
decision (one of: accept | partial_fill | reject)
recentAssistantMessages: Try mapping inputs and outputs as separate sections. The decision field is the most important — what triggers each state?

cases.name: 4-paste-of-llm-message
cases._intent: User pasted a recent assistant message verbatim → must fail with paste_detected=true.

plan.objective: Sketch the architecture in your own words.

micro_proof.stimulus: Describe the architecture you just heard about, in your own writing.

cases.response: An auth system typically separates request handling, validation, and persistence into distinct layers. The handler receives the request, validator checks tokens, persister stores state.
recentAssistantMessages: An auth system typically separates request handling, validation, and persistence into distinct layers. The handler receives the request, validator checks tokens, persister stores state.

cases.name: 5-paste-with-trivial-edits
cases._intent: User pasted with minor word swaps (~10% diff) → must fail (similarity ≥ 0.70).

plan.objective: Restate the workflow in your own framing.

micro_proof.stimulus: Restate the workflow logic in your own words.

cases.response: Each workflow step takes inputs from the previous stage and emits outputs to the next. The decision field decides whether the order proceeds. Quantity vs stock determines the outcome.
recentAssistantMessages: Each workflow step receives inputs from the previous stage and emits outputs to the next. The decision field determines whether the order proceeds. Quantity versus stock determines the outcome.
